html:
Nothing better than a rainy week to talk a bit about equipment.

My latest photographs were taken with a Sky90 II refractor from the Japanese firm Takahashi. Equipped with an apochromatic objective (which corrects colors) with a Fluorite doublet of 90mm diameter (F/D 5.6), its focal length is 500 mm, which is perfect for wide-field photography.

Compact, light, the build quality is impeccable. The dew shield is removable. A Takahashi 6X30 finder, which is also fantastic, can be added to it.

The refractor is paired with a focal reducer / field flattener (not potato fields). In this configuration, the refractor's focal length goes to 407 mm (f 4.5). With the Canon 40D, the field is then 3 degrees by 2 degrees and the field curvature is reasonable, with slight distortion of the stars at the edges of the images.
